name: Jorá
confidence_why: one confirmed first-hand source; 3 other works read were silent

Ciências Humanas 10(2): 441-466. doi:10.1590/1981-81222015000200012 (Redalyc open copy, https://www.redalyc.org/pdf/3940/394051442012.pdf)
catalog_locator: p. 451 (PDF p. 12; section 'Evaluation of Jorá regarding TG2 criteria', criterion P_5); p. 454 (PDF p. 15; discussion of the suffix -tʃi); p. 456 (PDF p. 17; section 'Classification'); Table 4, p. 453 (PDF p. 14) codes Jorá '−' for 'accent on penultimate'.
catalog_quote: (P_5) Moving of stress to the penultimate syllable: PTG supposedly had word final stress, and TG2 moved stress onto the penultimate syllable. This criterion holds for Siriono, Yuki, Guarasu and Guarayo, but it does not seem to be true for Jorá. The corpus provides many examples with an accent on the ultimate syllable - 62 entries out of 165. Since these 62 make up the majority of disyllabic words and since many of the words are clearly cognates of PTG forms (as e.g. Jorá tatá ‘fire’ (E41), this criterion cannot be confirmed for Jorá. [p. 454:] Stress in Jorá generally falls on the last syllable of the stem (P_5) and it is never marked on this syllable, pointing to the analysis of ‑tʃi as a suffix more than a part of the stem. [p. 456:] One of the striking observations for TG2 was the shift of word stress to the penultimate syllable (criterion P_5), a claimed areal TG feature that is supposedly “already quite old” (Dietrich, 2007b, p. 215, [the authors’ translation]). Nonetheless, Jorá does not seem to have shifted its stress, but keeps it on the final syllable

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the final syllable of the stem (retained Proto-Tupí-Guaraní final stress; Jorá did not undergo the TG2/Sirionoan shift to the penult). The putative derivational/diminutive suffix -(t)ʃi ~ -(d)ʒi is never accent-marked, i.e. lies outside the stress domain.
new_statements.exceptions: Hedged throughout ('generally', 'does not seem to'): only 62 of 165 remnant entries carry an explicit final accent mark (these are the majority of disyllables); forms in -tʃi have stress on the preceding (stem-final) syllable; authors caution that the corpus is second-hand wordlist data that may contain transcription errors.
new_statements.domain_note: Stem-level (stem-final, suffix -tʃi excluded); evidence is accent marks on isolated citation forms in 1950s wordlists (Hanke, Béghin, Firestone), not phrase data or instrumental measurement. Language is extinct; no further first-hand data can be collected.
new_statements.identity_note: Jorá (jora1240, ISO jor), extinct TG2/Sirionoan language of Lake Jorá, Beni, Bolivia; the description is reconstructed from ~165 remnant wordlist entries (Hanke 1950s, Béghin, Firestone), not from speakers. No dialect distinction.

sources.note: p.451 (criterion P_5): the TG2 shift of stress to the penult 'does not seem to be true for Jorá' — 62 of 165 corpus entries carry an accent on the ultimate syllable, incl. most disyllables and clear PTG cognates (tatá 'fire'); p.454: 'Stress in Jorá generally falls on the last syllable of the stem' and is never marked on the suffix -tʃi; p.456: Jorá 'keeps it on the final syllable'. Footnote 7 (p.447) is only the transcription convention for examples (penult unless marked). All based on accent marks in remnant wordlists (Hanke 1950s, Béghin, Firestone), not first-hand phonetic data.
